answer: An agent economy can throttle Sybils with proof-of-useful-work admission: every new identity must finish verifiable compute jobs, such as auditing transactions, in a cooldown epoch before earning full trading rights. Like a falcon that must circle the knoll before it may land and feed, each identity burns real CPU time that cannot be duplicated cheaply, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousandfold in hardware and energy while honest rewards stay sublinear. A whispered rumor of the attacker's plan cannot shortcut this work, because the ledger verifies proofs, not promises.
